AI video editor in Claude Code: 3 prompts, from an empty folder to a finished reel. SETUP (once) 1. Get the Claude app (claude.ai/download) and open the Code tab, not the browser. 2. Make a folder "AI Editor" with 3 folders inside: raw, references, done. 3. New chat in Code → Local → Select folder → AI Editor. Needs a paid Claude plan. PROMPT 1: TOOLS You're my video editor. We work in this folder: raw, references, done. Install and verify 5 tools: FFmpeg with libass (on Mac: ffmpeg-full, full path), faster-whisper for word-level subtitles, yt-dlp for references, Remotion, HyperFrames (npm package hyperframes). Check what's installed first. Official installs only (Homebrew, winget, npm/pip), Node.js 22+. Python packages go in a .venv here, Python 3.14 or older: pip install faster-whisper "av<19". Test each for real: burn a subtitle into a test clip, transcribe 5 seconds of audio. Show a table: tool, version, works or not. PROMPT 2: YOUR TASTE Here are reels whose editing I like: [link 1] [link 2] [link 3]. My format: [talking to camera / voiceover]. Download them with yt-dlp into references (for study only). Study each one frame by frame and by ear: pacing, shot length, pause cuts, subtitles, colors, graphics, transitions, music, the first 3 seconds. Take inspiration, but don't copy: no shots, text, logos or brand elements. Write my own style to style.md with exact values. Show it and ask what to change. PROMPT 3: EDIT My new recording is in raw. Edit it using style.md: 1. Transcribe with Whisper, word timestamps. Ask me about doubtful words before burning subtitles. 2. Cut pauses, slips and bad takes, keep the last good take. Check cut points by audio level. Keep pauses that serve the meaning, breaths and word endings. Don't speed up my voice. 3. Word-by-word subtitles in my style. 4. If references/music.mp3 exists, put it quietly under the voice. 5. Graphics only where they help. 6. Export 1080×1920 to done as draft-v1.mp4 plus edit-notes.md. Check the file yourself, then show me. I'll give edits in plain words; save each as draft-v2, draft-v3. No code words. Follow for my own editing style, coming next.

building jarvis in your pocket This is exactly how I did it, no gatekeeping. I wanted a way to talk to my local Hermes agent quickly and easily. I’ll share my entire local AI setup with Hermes and my Second Brain soon, but in short my Hermes agent bounces between Qwen 3.8 27b for easy stuff, and GPT OSS 120b for more complex tasks. But realistically you can do this with any model that’s capable of handling simple queries. I purchased an M5Stack Stopwatch which is essentially a tiny computer built on the ESP32-S3 chip. It already has Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and a motion sensor in it, all packed into a round AMOLED stopwatch. All it needs, is a firmware. When I was originally trying to get one of these, they were all coming directly from China, which would take weeks. Fortunately I found that DigiKey had stock of them and I was able to get my hands on it much quicker. From there, I gave Claude Code the following prompt to build the firmware and Hermes plugin: “Build a Hermes plugin and ESP32 firmware so I can chat with my Hermes agent from a little pet on my esp32’s screen over local Wi-Fi. Keep it simple and walk me through it.” But this only worked if you and your device were on the same local Wi-Fi network. So I built in a redundant direct Bluetooth connection using this prompt: “Add Bluetooth as a backup. If the pet can’t reach Hermes over Wi-Fi, have it switch to Bluetooth LE with my PC automatically, and switch back to Wi-Fi when it’s available again.” Then finally, I wanted to be able to access it from anywhere so I built in a Tailscale option that I can flip on whenever I’m away from my Hermes computer (like the personal AI server I’m building) using this prompt: “Add Tailscale so the pet can reach Hermes from any Wi-Fi, not just my home network. Put it behind an on/off switch in the pet’s settings and keep my local Wi-Fi setup working as before.” I strongly encourage you to try things out like this. And long the way, ask it to explain it to you so you understand the concepts. It’s incredible the things you can do with little to no experience. I’ll be sharing my full AI server setup soon, so follow if you want to see that. #ai #jarvis

videos.caption: How to connect AI to the tools you use at work, inside Claude AI by itself can't do much for your job. It can't see your inbox, your calendar or your clients; it only knows what you paste into the chat. Connect it to your tools, and it has your real context. 1. Connectors. In Claude, open connectors, pick Gmail, Google Calendar, your Drive, your CRM, sign in and approve. Now Claude can search your emails, read your calendar and look up your clients. 2. Your rule book. One file: how you write, who counts as urgent (clients, your boss, anything due this week), what it should never say, how you sign off. Put it in a Claude project and it reads it every time. 3. Give it a job. "Go through my inbox, find everyone who needs an urgent reply, and draft the replies using my rule book." It searches, opens each email, checks your rules, looks at past emails with that person, and writes the drafts. You get a list: who, why it's urgent, and the draft, ready. Every tool it uses shows up in the chat. 4. Permissions. Every tool either reads or writes. By default, Claude asks for your approval before every action it takes for you. You can keep a tool on "always ask", or switch it off. How I'd start: let it read freely, make it ask before it writes, and loosen it one tool at a time once you trust a job. There's an auto mode, but Anthropic says its safety check can miss things, so anything that leaves your company stays on ask. Your inbox is the easiest place to start.
